title: Lockstep Burst Profiling and Regression Watcher for TP/PP Workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run deterministic lockstep burst experiments targeting tensor-pipeline (TP/PP) mixed deployments to capture tokens/sec, p95 latency under microburst conditions, and cross-node KV warmup effects. Purpose is to create a reproducible baseline and an automated regression-watcher that flags >10% p95 regressions or >15% tokens/sec degradation during bursts compared to a rolling control window. This ticket covers harness design, telemetry schema, statistical detector tuning, and an initial nightly job to run the suite across two representative cluster profiles (homogeneous 8xA100, heterogeneous 4xA100+4xA10x).
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic harness that can replay a configured burst profile (requests/sec time series, input token length distribution, KV preheat state) and output per-step metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, inter-token spacing.
Nightly job that runs the suite against two cluster profiles and writes results to the benchmarks S3 bucket with schema versioned; artifacts include raw traces and aggregate summaries.

Regression watcher implemented: compares current run to 28-day rolling baseline using robust statistics (median + MAD) and emits alerts when p95 increases >10% or tokens/sec drops >15%; alerts show diff, percentile breakdown, and suggested suspects (kv-hit-rate, batch-size change, kernel fallback).
Dashboard tile (Console) that visualizes burst profiles, historical p95 trendlines, and per-run artifacts with link to PRs and commit hashes used for the run.
Smoke tests: harness validated on local 2-node dev cluster and on staging distributed cluster; results reproducible within 5% tokens/sec variance across 3 runs.
test_plan: Design burst scenarios: microburst (10s@200RPS), burst storm (60s ramp 0->500RPS), sustained surge (10m@75% capacity). Include mixed token length buckets: short(<=32), medium(33-256), long(>256).
KV preheat modes: cold (no kv), warm (prefix cache populated), sticky (kv pinned). Run each burst scenario across the three preheat modes.
Run each scenario on: homogeneous 8xA100 (tensor-only), heterogeneous 4xA100+4xA10x (mixed kernel fallback), and pipe-parallel 16-stage chain to exercise PP scheduling.
Collect telemetry: per-request timing, per-node GPU/GPU-mem utilization, kernel selection logs, batch composition histograms, and KV hit/miss counters.
Repeat runs: 3 repeats per scenario to measure variance; aggregate median and MAD for baseline creation.
telemetry: Captured fields: run_id, cluster_profile, commit_sha, model_name, model_variant, burst_profile_id, preheat_mode, sample_start_ts, sample_end_ts.
Per-step metrics: tokens_sec, requests_sec, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, avg_batch_size, kv_hit_rate, gpu_util_percent, mem_util_percent, inter_arrival_cv.
Log retention: raw traces (7 days), aggregated summaries (90 days). Upload objects to s3://redwood-benchmarks/lockstep/2026-02/ with jsonl and parquet summaries.
Normalization: attach measured hardware counters and environment tags to enable apples-to-apples comparisons.
regression_detection: Detection algorithm: compare current-run median and p95 to 28-day rolling baseline using median and MAD; flag if p95_current > p95_baseline*(1+threshold) or tokens_sec_current < tokens_sec_baseline*(1-threshold). Default thresholds: p95 +10%, tokens/sec -15%.
Noise filtering: require regression to be present in >=2 of 3 scenario repeats and not solely explained by kv_hit_rate drop >20% unless kv preheat config changed.
Notification: create alert in Slack channel #bench-alerts with run links, diff table, and suggested suspects (e.g., kernel_fallback_ratio increased, batch_size shift, cross-node traffic imbalance).
Autocapture suspects: run lightweight diff analysis script to compute per-node delta of gpu_util and per-batch kernel usage; include top-3 anomalies in alert.
